newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.S. CIA chief meets Indonesia's Suharto.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CIA chief meets Indonesia's Suharto.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto met the director of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), John Deutch, on Thursday for talks, officials said.

Deutch refused to comment on what was discussed but the head of Indonesia's intelligence services, Mutojib, said talks had been arranged after the CIA requested a meeting with Suharto to obtain a first-hand account of political developments in Indonesia.
"They (the CIA) wanted to get to know the situation here, because until now they have only heard comment from parties that want to discredit Indonesia," Mutojib told reporters.
"President Suharto has explained to him (Deutch) of the need of national stability," Mutojib said.
He added that Deutch was the first director of the CIA to visit Indonesia, one of several countries including China and South Korea where the CIA chief has held talks during a tour of Asia.
The government has blamed a student's group which it says is patterned on the banned Communist Party of Indonesia for riots in Jakarta in July, the worst violence in the city for over two decades.

The riots erupted after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) to evict supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri, who had been ousted from the party leadership by a government-backed faction in June.

The United States said after the riots it was concerned that a crackdown by Indonesian authorities could lead to criminal proceedings against opponents of the government. It had said all those detained should be given due process.
